title: Top Down Proteomics Data Collection for Microdissected Kidney Tissue Functional Units
author: James M Fulcher
materials: To quickly evaluate the QC data, open them in the Thermo Scientific Freestyle software or Xcalibur QualBrowser. The following metrics are inspected to ensure that the LCMS run meets the expected standard.

Evaluation of QC data ( Shewanella lysate from section 3) To quickly evaluate the QC data, open them in the Thermo Scientific Freestyle software or Xcalibur QualBrowser. The following metrics are inspected to ensure that the LCMS run meets the expected standard. 1. Signal levels The intensity levels at the total ion current (TIC), base peak intensity (BPI), and the MS2 spectra are inspected to ensure that they meet the expected intensity levels. The TIC intensity levels are typically expected to be above the 1e10 level, BPI at or above 1e8 level, and the MS2 spectra ion current from 1e5 to 1e7 levels. 2. Chromatography 2a. We look at the chromatography distribution using the base peak FTMS scan as filter to ensure that the eluted peaks are well distributed through the LC run. The chromatogram is filtered to show the BPI peaks and inspected to ensure no peak broadening (early or late) is observed. Chromatogram filtered using the BPI to show the peak distribution. 2b. The distribution of the MS2 peaks (fragmentation of peaks selected at the MS1 level) is inspected to evaluate how similar the distribution is to that of the MS1 level. The MS2 distribution is expected to emulate what is observed for the peak distribution of the MS1 when the BPI filter is applied, indicating that peak selection for fragmentation was performed at an appreciable level. To assess the MS2 fragmentation signal, the “full MS2” is applied as the filter to show the MS2 distribution through the whole experiment. 2c. Finally, QC samples are analyzed with TopPIC to ensure appropriate number of proteoforms and proteoform spectrum matches (PrSMs) are being identified. TopPIC Suite 1.4.13.1 https://github.com/toppic-suite/toppic-suite Xiaowen Liu Proteoforms are counted by opening the exported "..._proteoforms.tsv" file and PrSMs through the "..._PrSMs.tsv" file. The QC passing threshold for proteoforms is 1,000 and 2,000 for PrSMs.

steps.title: Set Up Reversed-Phase LC System
steps.instruction: Configure the reversed-phase LC system with online trapping for desalting using a NanoAcquity (Waters, 186016002) with autosampler 186016007 and a dual pump configuration.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Mobile phase A (MPA): 0.2% formic acid in LCMS grade water.
Prepare Mobile phase B (MPB): 0.2% formic acid in LCMS grade acetonitrile.

steps.title: Calibrate Mass Spectrometer
steps.instruction: Calibrate and set up the mass spectrometer method following the instrument vendor's recommendations.

substeps.instruction: Complete 'positive polarity' and 'Orbitrap mass' calibrations.
Perform system calibration to ensure performance for ETD and 'Intact protein mode'.

steps.title: Enable Full Profile Mode (Optional)
steps.instruction: If desired, enable full profile mode to capture low abundance species by navigating to 'Diagnosis' -> 'System' -> 'Orbitrap' -> 'Utilities' and checking 'Toggle Full Profile Data' before starting the queue.

substeps.instruction: Note: This generates ~10 GB files per 100 min run.
Toggle off full profile mode after the queue to reset the instrument.

steps.title: Configure Data Dependent Acquisition Method
steps.instruction: Set up the data dependent acquisition method for the Orbitrap Fusion Lumos with the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Global Settings: Method Duration 100 min, Spray Voltage Static, Gas Mode Static, Infusion Mode (LC) False, FAIMS Not Installed, Application Mode Intact Protein, Pressure Mode Low Pressure, Default Charge State 6, Advanced Peak Determination True.

Experiment 1 (MS): Start 0 min, End 100 min, MasterScan (min points across peak 6, MSn Level 1, Wide Quad Isolation True, Detector Orbitrap, Resolution 120K, Mass Range Normal, Scan Range 500-2000 m/z, Max Injection Time 500 ms, AGC Target 1,000,000, Normalized AGC Target 250%, Microscans 4, Max Injection Time Type Custom, RF Lens 30%, ETD Internal Calibration False, DataType Profile, Polarity Positive, Source Fragmentation True, Energy 15V, Enhanced Resolution Mode Off).

MS Filter: ChargeState 3-35, Include undetermined charge states False, DynamicExclusion (Exclude after 1 time, Duration 30s, Mass tolerance low/high 1 mz), Exclude isotopes True, Perform dependent scan on single charge state per precursor only True.
Data Dependent Properties: Mode Number of Scans, Number of Dependent Scans 1 (sample run) or 8 (library run).

Scan Event 1 (ddMSnScan): Min points across peak 6, MSn Level 2, Isolation Mode Quadrupole, Intelligent Product Acquisition False, Isolation Window 2, Isolation Offset Off, Reported Mass Original Mass, Multi-notch Isolation False, Scan Range Mode Auto, Scan Priority 1, Collision Energy Mode Fixed, ActivationType CID, Collision Energy 35%, Activation Time 10 ms, Activation Q 0.25, Multistage Activation False, Detector Orbitrap, Resolution 60K, Max Injection Time 200 ms, AGC Target 500,000, Inject ions for all parallelizable time False, Normalized AGC Target 1000%, Microscans 1, Max Injection Time Type Custom, ETD Internal Calibration False, DataType Profile, Polarity Positive, Source Fragmentation False, Time Mode Unscheduled, Enhanced Resolution Mode Off.

steps.title: Set Up Gradient Method
steps.instruction: Configure the LC gradient and wash pump settings for samples.

substeps.instruction: Wash pump: 5 μL/min, 95% MPA, 5% MPB; Loading time 10 min.
Gradient pump: 0.3 μL/min.
0 min: 95% MPA, 5% MPB.
1 min: 90% MPA, 10% MPB.
90 min: 40% MPA, 60% MPB.
100 min: 95% MPA, 5% MPB.

steps.title: Adjust Autosampler for microPOTS Samples
steps.instruction: Adjust the needle placement in the nanoACQUITY Sample Manager Software to accommodate PCR tubes inside LC vials.

substeps.instruction: Select the autosampler and go to 'advanced' options.
Check the 'Needle Placement (from bottom)' box.
Set needle placement to 10.2 mm from the bottom of the LC vial.

steps.title: Prepare QC Standard
steps.instruction: Prepare a bacterial lysate (e.g., Shewanella oneidensis MR-1) to evaluate instrument performance.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Homogenization buffer (HB): 8M urea (480 mg/mL) in 50 mM ABC with 15 mM TCEP (using BondBreaker 0.5 M TCEP stock).
Prepare Wash Buffer (WB): 0.2% formic acid, 5% acetonitrile in LC-MS grade water.
Lyse cells or homogenize tissue in HB and incubate at room temperature for 30 min.
Centrifuge lysate at 14,000 x G, 10°C for 10 minutes to pellet debris.
Transfer supernatant to 100K MWCO filter and centrifuge at 14,000 x G to minimum volume.
Wash 100K spin filter with 1X max volume of HB, spin at 14,000 x G to minimum volume.
Transfer filtrate to a 10K filter and centrifuge at 14,000 x G to minimum volume (add multiple aliquots if needed).
Wash 10K filter three times with WB, spinning to minimum volume each time.
Perform Coomassie or BCA protein assay.
Dilute sample to 0.01 ug/uL in WB and aliquot 100 uL into labeled 0.6 mL Eppendorf tubes.

steps.title: Run QC and Sample Queues
steps.instruction: Execute the QC run before proceeding to sample runs.

substeps.instruction: Queue the QC using the QC LCMS method (Method Duration 90 min, Default Charge State 10, MS MasterScan Max Injection Time 400 ms, Microscans 2, ChargeState 4-35, Number of Dependent Scans 4, ddMSnScan Scan Range 400-2000 m/z, Microscans 2).
Verify that QC runs pass defined metrics.
Once passed, queue the sample runs using the LCMS method described in the acquisition setup.

steps.title: Perform Proteoform Identification and Filtering
steps.instruction: Process the raw data to identify and filter proteoforms.

substeps.instruction: Perform proteoform identification using the TopPIC processing protocol.
Filter kidney samples based on TopPIC PrSM results (after TopPICR post-processing), removing samples with fewer than 100 PrSMs.
